propositions: Multiple bundles for a single S3 ref cause clone to hard-fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed' and push to stall indefinitely because git-remote-s3 rejects writes while bundles>1 before any attempt to resolve the divergence

Upstream git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() calls) and discards non-chosen heads by default, losing unique ticket events that are unacceptable in an append-only event log

The heal must write a merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any original bundle and never delete the merged tip, guaranteeing at least one bundle carrying full merged history remains after any crash

The heal folds N divergent heads via iterated 2-parent git merges following rebar's existing lossless reconcile semantics, unioning unrelated-history heads via --allow-unrelated-histories, and aborting only on genuine content conflicts

Detection and one-attempt healing in push.py's non-FF handler ensures push convergence under contention, as the shared remote's single-bundle collapse is visible to all competing processes on their next push retry

All S3 access (lock, enumerate, delete) routes through git-remote-s3's own S3Remote and boto3 client, adding no direct S3 dependency to core rebar (boto3 transitive under optional [s3] extra) and reusing the helper's private API behind a thin adapter
